readings.wow: w/w easing — retreating from 4-month highs, settling into 57–58/MWh range
readings.source: Front-month at ~€57.55/MWh on 28 Jul (per tradingeconomics.com/commodity/eu-natural-gas search snippet; direct page returned 403), up 1.52% on the day — easing back from the ~€59.39 four-month high of 21 Jul. ICE TTF had been 58.91 EUR/MWh as of 17 Jul. EU storage at 54.2% full vs 65% a year ago per search snippets. Ongoing Hormuz disruption (Qatari tanker attack 7 Jul, Hormuz transits collapsed) continues to underpin elevated levels. Still within existing €57–60/MWh range; week-on-week direction has shifted from sharply rising to easing.

editorialReading: TTF has edged back from last week's four-month high — but the conditions driving EU nitrogen plant-idling pressure have not changed. Front-month gas pulled back to approximately €57.55/MWh on 28 July, retreating from the ~€59.39 peak of 21 July, yet EU storage stands at just 54.2% full versus 65% a year ago, leaving the continent acutely exposed to any further Hormuz escalation. Above €57/MWh the production economics for European ammonia remain structurally challenged: BASF, Yara, and OCI face the same import-parity calculus as in prior high-gas episodes, and the modest week-on-week retreat offers no genuine relief at this level. Urea has consolidated its recovery from the mid-July trough, with CBOT FOB Egypt Aug-26 futures holding near ~$475/t — the sharp rebound from ~$385–400 appears to be stabilising, suggesting the Hormuz war premium and Egypt's ad valorem duty release have reached a temporary equilibrium. The July Tampa ammonia contract is confirmed at ~$800/t; August settlement remains pending. With gas sustained above €57/MWh and urea re-priced well above pre-crisis levels, EU nitrogen economics continue to be squeezed from both the feedstock and import-competition sides simultaneously, deepening the continent's dependence on non-European supply through the autumn 2026 application window.
watchNext: Whether TTF sustains above €57/MWh into the autumn 2026 application window — if so, EU plant-idling pressure returns and import dependence deepens. Whether August Tampa ammonia settles above July's ~$800/t on continued North African tightening and the renewed Hormuz premium. Whether urea consolidates in the ~$450–475/t range or resumes its climb. India / China urea tender activity and any export curbs remain the physical swing factor. Sourcing note: real-time Argus / ICIS / Green Markets assessments are subscription-only and the free World Bank Pink Sheet lags ~a month — these are publicly-cited indications.
